STEEP HIGH-ANGLE VIEW FROM ABOVE AND SLIGHTLY IN FRONT, exactly as the game RimWorld draws its trees and standing lamps: we look mostly DOWN onto the object's top; its height is strongly foreshortened, so only a short strip of its front shows below the top; its foot at the BOTTOM of the canvas and its top towards the TOP. No side-on view, no isometric angle, no tilt.

Create an ORIGINAL game building sprite for a whip antenna: a small dual-band radio antenna on a short steel pole, put up outside a hard-scrabble frontier colony's radio room. Image 1 is our approved parts bench from the same maker: match its outline weight, shading, palette and finish only. Do NOT copy its shape, contents.

Portrait canvas. The antenna fills about 80 percent of the canvas height, centred, on a plain pure white background.

Seen steeply from above: a small square concrete footing at the bottom; a short foreshortened galvanised steel pole rising from it; at its top, a small round grey connector housing, from which four thin stiff rods spread out and down like the ribs of an open umbrella, making a clear X-shaped star when seen from above; from the centre of the housing, one thin rod pointing up, foreshortened, with a small ball tip. A black cable runs down the pole to the footing.

Style: a sprite for the game RimWorld: a thick near-black outline around every shape, soft flat cel shading with two or three tones per material, muted grey steel, a few small clean details, no texture noise. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not pixel art.

No text, letters, numbers, logos, lamps, lights, flags, birds, people, wires to anything else, ground beyond the footing, shadow outside the antenna, landscape or sky.
